Deep learning techniques of MLP and CNN are applied to predict the tool faults with possible variations in working conditions and system characteristics. Then, a hybrid deep learning algorithm of MLP-CNN is also used to indicate the wear of the drill bit tool. After applying deep learning techniques with the integration of digital twins and Principal Component Analysis (PCA), a comparative analysis was done in the final stage to conclude the effectiveness of the proposed model. The experimental result says that DT with hybrid MLP-CNN is more accurate in predicting drill bit faults, with the highest accuracy of 100% with a limited amount of measured data.

articleTitle: Traffic-noise Annoyance Assessment Method Combining LSTM and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: This study is dedicated to developing a deep learning-based traffic noise signal evaluation method, with the goal of improving the accuracy and efficiency of noise evaluation and providing solid scientific support for urban planning and noise management. With the acceleration of urbanization, the interference of traffic noise on residents' daily lives is becoming increasingly significant, and the evaluation of traffic noise has gradually received widespread attention from researchers. This paper proposes a traffic noise annoyance assessment model that combines Long Short Term Memory Network (LSTM) and transfer learning. This method elaborates in detail on the working principle, structural design, selection of loss function, configuration of optimizer during training, and adjustment strategy of learning rate of the model. The experimental results show that compared with other methods, the evaluation model in this paper performs well in evaluation indicators such as mean absolute error, Pearson correlation coefficient, and Spearman correlation coefficient. In addition, the evaluation performance of the model in different annoyance degree intervals also reaches a high level.

articleTitle: Augmenting Short Sequence for Robust Session-based Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: In recent years, recommendation systems leveraging deep neural networks have gained prominence as a means to address the information overload challenge exacerbated by the rapid advancement of the Internet. Predominantly, deep recommendation models focus on modeling user attribute features by utilizing the sequence of previously interacted items to predict the next item a user is likely to engage with. However, prior to user registration or login on an application, these recommendation models can only access a limited scope of user interactions, typically restricted to a short sequence of recent sessions. This brevity inherently constrains the accuracy of the recommendation model. To mitigate this limitation, we draw inspiration from the concept of sequence augmentation in contrastive learning, which employs short sequences to derive additional supervised signals based on association rules. Furthermore, we incorporate the notion of non-negative transfer learning to enhance the extraction of supervised signals that better align with the underlying intent of user sessions. Comprehensive experiments conducted on three real-world datasets substantiate the efficacy of our proposed model, demonstrating its superiority over traditional RNN, CNN, GNN, and various Transformer-based approaches.

articleTitle: Large Language Models for Government Document Writing: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has had a significant impact on fields such as question answering (Q&A) and machine understanding. However, due to the specificity of government documents, there are several LLMs exclusively focused on government document writing. In this survey, we thoroughly examine the application of LLMs in the creation and refinement of government documents. A systematic comparison of various models, i.e., ChatGPT-4 and Kimi, is provided here. Our findings reveal that, although LLMs can significantly streamline the document preparation process, there is considerable variation in their effectiveness. ChatGPT-4 stands out as the top-performing model, excelling in context understanding and grammatical accuracy, followed closely by QWen2.5. In contrast, TinyLlama performs limited comprehension of Chinese and exhibits a propensity for English output. This survey has two main contributions: (1) emphasizes the importance of the task of polishing government documents; (2) fills the gap in the market for a comprehensive comparison of LLMs in the task of polishing government documents. Through comparison analysis, this paper aims at giving a reference for future research and practical application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the government sector. At the same time, it can assure the maximum of potential and lower the risks of it.

articleTitle: Research on Exchange Rate Prediction Driven by Multi-Source Heterogeneous Data: Based on Retrieval Augmented Generation and Explainable Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: With the accelerating pace of global economic integration, exchange rate fluctuations have been influenced by various uncertain factors. The information explosion has further complicated the factors influencing exchange rate predictions. To fully utilize multi-source heterogeneous data and further optimize exchange rate prediction performance, this paper constructs an exchange rate prediction method based on Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence models. During the data processing stage, this paper first uses RAG technology to enhance the situational learning ability of Large Language Models (LLMs). By combining prompts and local sentiment databases, LLMs can perform real-time and accurate sentiment analysis on news headlines. Secondly, transfer learning is used to optimize the Inception(v3) model for sentiment analysis of news images, thereby more efficiently analyzing the sentiment variables contained in texts and images, effectively enriching the sources of multi-source heterogeneous data. Extensive experiments have shown that the multi-source heterogeneous dataset constructed in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy of exchange rate predictions and improve the predictive performance of various models across different time steps.

articleTitle: Target Detection of Safety Protective Gear Using the Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: In high-risk railway construction, personal protective equipment monitoring is critical but challenging due to small and frequently obstructed targets. We propose YOLO-EA, an innovative model that enhances safety measure detection by integrating ECA into its backbone's convolutional layers, improving discernment of minuscule objects like hardhats. YOLO-EA further refines target recognition under occlusion by replacing GIoU with EIoU loss. YOLO-EA's effectiveness was empirically substantiated using a dataset derived from real-world railway construction site surveillance footage. It outperforms YOLOv5, achieving 98.9% precision and 94.7% recall, up 2.5% and 0.5% respectively, while maintaining real-time performance at 70.774 fps. This highly efficient and precise YOLO-EA holds great promise for practical application in intricate construction scenarios, enforcing stringent safety compliance during complex railway construction projects.

articleTitle: Modeling the Competitive Content Service Market from the Perspective of Consumer Preferences: A Game Theory Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Deploying interaction-intensive AI-generated content (AIGC) services on mobile edge networks enables mobile AIGC to deliver personalized, high-quality content efficiently and cost-effectively. These services are designed to automatically generate content based on user inputs or requirements, positioning mobile AIGC as a promising solution for content creation in immersive and dynamic Metaverse environments. However, the current implementation of edge devices as AIGC Service Providers (ASPs) suffers from a lack of incentives, which impedes the sustainable delivery of high-quality edge AIGC services. This paper tries to design an incentive strategy by investigating the competition relationship among AIGC service providers (ASPs) as a Duopoly Game, which mathematically describes the competition among ASPs based on their service quality, cost, and prices. In this content service market, social planners issue policies to improve social welfare while providers maximize their profits according to the consumption preference of users. This consumption preference of consumers is described as consumer preference model to capture consumers' demands for different QoS services when different content service providers serve them simultaneously. The simulation shows that 1) competition among providers will produce more differences on content service quality than social regulation will bring; 2) more social welfare may be engendered by the competition among different ASPs.

articleTitle: Beyond Photometric Constraints: Epipolar-Based Self-Supervised Learning for Visual Odometry
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced self-supervised learning (SSL) framework for Visual Odometry (VO), aiming to improve pose and depth estimation in dynamic and complex environments. The proposed approach integrates three key innovations: a unified loss function, selective photometric loss, and adaptive geometric constraints. The unified loss dynamically adjusts the balance between photometric and geometric terms based on scene dynamics, ensuring accurate depth and pose predictions. The selective photometric loss focuses only on stable texture regions, reducing errors from reflections, occlusions, and moving objects. Adaptive geometric constraints refine pose estimation by leveraging robust key point matching and epipolar geometry to minimize computational complexity while maintaining high accuracy. Our framework was evaluated extensively on the KITTI dataset, achieving an RMSE of 5.564 and an absolute relative error (Abs Rel) of 0.152, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods across key metrics. The proposed architecture also features a streamlined encoder-decoder setup with skip connections, enabling efficient joint optimization of depth and pose while reducing network complexity. Qualitative results highlight significant improvements in depth map consistency and pose estimation, particularly in challenging scenarios with high motion and dynamic objects. This work contributes to the field by addressing key limitations in self-supervised VO, such as sensitivity to dynamic objects and computational inefficiency, while demonstrating robust performance for real-world applications. The proposed framework is scalable, computationally efficient, and suitable for real-time applications, such as autonomous driving and robotics. Future research will explore integrating additional modalities, such as optical flow, to further enhance accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Class-level Alignment Domain Adaptation Method for Non-Destructive Testing of Transformer Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: In practical industrial applications, the fault diagnosis method based on artificial intelligence often has the problem of insufficient accuracy because of the distribution deviation between different signal sources. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a Class-level Alignment Domain Adaptation(CADA). In CADA, we introduce a distribution alignment module based on optimal transmission (OT) to eliminate inter-domain differences in data from different domains. At the same time, to make the data distribution and category alignment closer, we use the feature fusion strategy to combine the feature information and label information. Then realize the joint alignment of the data distribution and category by aligning the fusion features of the two domains. Further, we use the dual form of Wasserstein distance to measure distribution differences, thus reducing the high time cost of traditional OT-based methods to measure distribution differences. We conducted comparison experiments based on real voiceprint monitoring data to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The experimental results demonstrate the promising performance of our approach.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Similarity-Driven Three-Way Decision Model of Rough Fuzzy Sets
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Three-way decision (3WD) theory provides an innovative approach to categorizing uncertain issues into acceptance, rejection, and non-commitment regions. The rough fuzzy sets (RFS) model extends rough sets to handle imprecise or fuzzy concepts. A critical challenge in developing the three-way decision model of rough fuzzy sets (3WDRFS) lies in determining and interpreting threshold pairs. However, the traditional expert-based subjective risk parameters often lead to significant misclassification errors in 3WD. To address this limitation, we propose a novel fuzzy similarity-driven 3WDRFS framework (3WDRFS-FS). Our approach involves two key steps: (1) developing a three-way approximation shadowed set (3WA-SS) model using average-step fuzzy sets (AFS), and (2) formulating an objective function to quantify the fuzzy similarity between AFS and 3WA-SS, which is utilized to derive the optimal threshold pair for the 3WDRFS-FS model. Relevant experimental results validate the effectiveness of our proposed model. Moreover, the 3WDRFS-FS model demonstrates superior performance compared to the 0.5-approximation model (0.5-AM).

articleTitle: CTTrack: Leveraging Cross-Transformer for Multi-Scale Feature Fusion in Multi-Object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Multi-object tracking is a fundamental and challenging task in the field of computer vision. Contemporary multi-object tracking methods mainly follow the detection-tracking paradigm, in which image features play a crucial role in tracking. However, most existing object tracking methods use displacement regression or motion estimation to determine object positions, which relegates the importance of features to a secondary role. Moreover, single feature information is insufficient to effectively distinguish similar objects. Therefore, this paper proposes CT-Track, a target tracker that integrates semantic and structural information. Specifically, we densely sample candidate regions of hundreds of objects in image pairs for contrastive learning and introduce a cross-transformer to fuse rich structural information from low-level features with semantic information from high-level features. This fusion enhances localization capabilities and the understanding of complex scenes, resulting in more robust tracking performance. Experiments on the MOT17 and joint datasets highlight the benefits of multi-scale feature fusion using cross-transformer in multi-object tracking.

articleTitle: Harmonizing Metadata of Language Resources for Enhanced Querying and Accessibility
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: This paper addresses the harmonization of meta-data from diverse repositories of language resources (LRs). Leveraging linked data and RDF techniques, we integrate data from multiple sources into a unified model based on DCAT and META-SHARE OWL ontology. Our methodology supports text-based search, faceted browsing, and advanced SPARQL queries through Linghub, a newly developed portal. Real user queries from the Corpora Mailing List (CML) were evaluated to assess Linghub’s capability to satisfy actual user needs. Results indicate that while some limitations persist, many user requests can be successfully addressed. The study highlights significant metadata issues and advocates for adherence to open vocabularies and standards to enhance metadata harmonization. This initial research underscores the importance of API-based access to LRs, promoting machine usability and data subset extraction for specific purposes, paving the way for more efficient and standardized LR utilization.

articleTitle: Video Fire Shape Deformation Identification Algorithm based on Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Real-time video detection of fire is widely used in fire prevention and security fields, allowing for timely fire warnings and reducing personal and property damage. Existing algorithms often adopt object detection models cascaded with other criteria to determine whether fire exists in video frames. These criteria are mostly limited to single-frame image features, which fail to effectively suppress false alarms caused by high-brightness interference objects (such as car headlights or streetlights at night). Therefore, this paper proposes a video fire shape deformation recognition algorithm, FireShapeCLR(Contrastive Learning Representation), based on self-supervised contrastive learning. Firstly, a sample collection strategy is proposed to construct anchor samples, positive samples, and negative samples triplets. Secondly, a feature extraction network is utilized to compute the feature of samples and calculate the cosine distance between the triplets. Finally, Info-NCE loss function is employed to drive model training. This algorithm effectively leverages the visual characteristic of high-frequency shape variations of fire in the time domain, combined with self-supervised contrastive learning, to address the limitation of traditional algorithms in determining whether an object has deformed, significantly reducing false alarm rates. Experimental results show that the cascaded FireShapeCLR algorithm can reduce the false alarm rate by 23% while maintaining the detection rate of the original model.

articleTitle: Wild Mushroom Image Segmentation Algorithm Based on Improved DeepLabV3+
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Wild mushrooms in China are diverse and widely distributed, particularly in southwestern regions like Yunnan and Guizhou, where many inedible species pose a risk of poisoning upon accidental ingestion. To mitigate these incidents, researchers are increasingly focused on species recognition. However, the natural growth environments of wild mushrooms introduce significant background disturbance, complicating accurate identification. Consequently, separating the background from the image is crucial for enhancing recognition accuracy. To solve the above problems, this paper takes the common wild mushrooms in Guizhou province as the research object and proposes a deep learning network based on the improved DeepLabV3+ for the background segmentation task of wild mushroom images. Firstly, the network Xception backbone feature extraction network of the original DeepLabV3+ is replaced with MobileNetV2 network, which makes the network more lightweight and suitable for deployment into mobile devices. Secondly, the Feature Pyramid Networks feature fusion branch is proposed to realize the fusion of different levels of feature maps, so that the network can extract richer wild mushroom features and improve the wild mushroom image segmentation accuracy. And then, a multi-layer cascade superposition is used to replace the original Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling module with Dense Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling as an enhanced feature extraction network to increase the perceptual field of the network and obtain the multi-scale information of the wild mushroom image. Finally, the ResNet-18 network was used to identify the segmented images. Experimental results show that the improved DeepLabV3+ has better segmentation performance. The average segmentation accuracy of the algorithm is 96.81%, the mean Intersection over Union is 92.36%, and the average accuracy after ResNet-18 recognition reaches 93.8%. In the comparison experiments, our segmentation algorithm has a higher segmentation accuracy and a lower model size. This method can provide technical support for automatic segmentation and identification of wild mushroom images in natural environment.

articleTitle: Military Fine-tuning Dataset Construction Method for Chinese Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have seen increasing utilization in various general fields. However, their application in the Chinese military domain has not yielded satisfactory results. A significant factor is that due to particularity of the military domain, acquisition of high-quality large-scale Chinese datasets is not only costly, but also extremely difficult during implement. Recently, a turning point has been reached in the construction of fine-tuning datasets for military-domain Chinese LLMs, that is, with the iteration of open-source Chinese LLMs, their reasoning capabilities have notably improved, enhancing the reliability of generated data. Besides, data generation methods based on LLMs are constantly emerging. The approach of leveraging the knowledge base and reasoning abilities of LLMs to generate datasets, subsequently fine-tuning the large models, has been validated multiple times.The motivation of this work is to explore the application of LLMs to generate large-scale fine-tuned datasets for the military domain. Furthermore, enhance the military knowledge base and reasoning capabilities of LLMs. In this work, we proposed three military data generation methods based on LLMs and conducted experiments on two of them. The experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the approach in generating large-scale military datasets and subsequently, fine-tuning large models. Additionally, we delved into the domain-transfer capabilities of LLMs, providing deeper insights into their potential and limitations.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Estimation with Evidential Regression for Lightweight Stereo Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Stereo matching is a significant part in many computer vision tasks, particularly in autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance systems. Even though existing stereo matching methods have achieved considerable progress, they often exhibit pronounced disparity jumps at edges and thin structures, and lack uncertainty estimation for the predicted disparity maps. These issues are crucial for ensuring the safe operation of vehicles. In this paper, we introduce a lightweight stereo matching architecture, which leverages deep evidence regression to simultaneously estimate disparity maps and their associated uncertainties. During this process, we effectively integrate contextual features, enhancing the performance on edge details. To improve real-time performance, we propose the Group Multi-axis Attention Volume (GMAV), a concise cost volume that uses correlation volumes as attention weights to refine feature volume processed by Group Multi-axis Attention Fusion (GMAF). Based on these two structures, we designed a stereo matching method called Uncertainty Estimation with Evidential Regression Network (UERNet). Experiments on SceneFlow and KITTI datasets demonstrate that our method achieves a good balance between speed and accuracy. Our network achieved a D1-all accuracy of 2.01% on the KITTI 2015 test set. This represents a 20% performance increase over the baseline model.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Approaches in CARLA’s Autonomous Driving Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: The convergence of sophisticated algorithms and evolving simulation platforms holds promise for advancements in autonomous driving. Employing the CARLA simulator, our research undertakes a comprehensive exploration of three cardinal Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms: A3C, DDQN, and DDPG. Our findings unearth distinct behavioral patterns and proficiencies. The DDPG, undeniably audacious, pushes for higher speeds, yet occasionally strays from the optimal path, especially in challenging curves. In contrast, A3C’s wavering trajectory in both training and unfamiliar environments signifies a more cautious approach. The real revelation, however, is the DDQN which, in a nuanced ballet of speed and precision, consistently holds a central trajectory, signaling a harmonious blend of speed and safety. Notably, the embrace of Variational Autoencoder (VAE), inspired by prior works demonstrating its efficacy in expediting training, serves as an auxiliary catalyst in our experiments. This synthesis offers invaluable insights for future endeavors aiming to refine driving strategies in ever-complicated urban terrains.

articleTitle: AI Strategies and Game Dynamics in Risk: Analyzing AI Personalities and Player Order Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: This paper explores the development and evaluation of artificial intelligence (AI) strategies in the board game Risk, focusing on algorithmic approaches to decision-making and the impact of player order on game outcomes. By modeling the game as a graph optimization problem, I develop AI personalities with distinct traits in threat perception, priority, placement, and attack strategies, resulting in 16 variations. The study introduces algorithms for troop placement and fortification, aiming to achieve a center-weak border-strong distribution of armies. Analysis of gameplay data reveals trends related to player order, with certain AI personalities exhibiting advantages based on their order of play. Notably, an AI with a defensive and cautious strategy demonstrates a unique advantage when playing second. The findings suggest strategies for human players and highlight areas for future research, including subgraph analysis and dynamic game shifts, to enhance AI decision-making in Risk.

articleTitle: Curriculum Vitae Sorting: A Novel Framework for Personality-based Automatic CV Sorting using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Both skill and personality play impactful roles in professional performance. The Human Resource Management (HRM) identifies and verifies the skill set and academic background while recruiting new employees. However, analyzing the personalities of the applicants is challenging. Because humans have intrinsic characteristics that allow them to express fabricated personalities in different settings. Nevertheless, people frequently express their true sentiments on social media. This paper presents an innovative and effective framework, the Curriculum Vitae Sorting (CVS) framework, that uses Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) dataset to identify the personalities of job applicants using their social media posts. The CVS framework achieves a remarkable 92.88% classification accuracy with a 4.55% False Positive Rate (FPR). The practical application of this framework demonstrates an 11.67% improvement in the Key Performance Indicator (KPI) among newly recruited employees. The 0.9311% precision, 0.9294% recall, and 0.9403% F1-score of the CVS framework demonstrate its outstanding and reliable performance in personality classification. This unique application of Deep Learning (DL) in HRM unearths a new dimension of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in business, helping organizations recruit employees with the required personalities and qualities.

articleTitle: Autonomous Driving Algorithm Based on Relative Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: The human-set reward function in traditional autonomous driving algorithms based on reinforcement learning is subjective and empirical, and it cannot accurately reflect the degree of influence of various factors on driving strategy. To overcome the aforementioned issues, an automated driving system based on relative entropy inverse reinforcement learning is presented. First, using the relative entropy inverse reinforcement learning algorithm, the a priori knowledge of human drivers is extracted from their driving trajectory data and quantitatively described as a reward function. The learned reward function is then incorporated into the policy gradient-based reinforcement learning algorithm, which directs the training of the autonomous vehicles to continuously update their driving strategy in a direction similar to that of the human driver. The experimental results show that the autonomous vehicle can learn the human driver’s prior knowledge using an autonomous driving algorithm based on relative entropy inverse reinforcement learning and that the reward function restored by this method can better reflect the degree of influence of various factors on the driving strategy.

articleTitle: Real Time lane detection system using Computer Vision techniques with Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Since accurate lane recognition is the cornerstone of autonomous driving and, in most situations, a matter of life or death, it is essential for a wide range of computer vision applications in driving systems. There is still room to investigate the nuances of lane recognition and strategies for improving its effectiveness, even with the current state of development. In order to identify lane boundaries from video streams. This study presents a dynamic lane detection system with real-time adaptability, integrating cutting-edge techniques such as perspective transformations, polynomial regression, edge detection, gradient analysis, and object detection. Our approach demonstrates encouraging results through dataset testing and evaluation, underscoring its potential for real-time application in autonomous vehicles and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS).

articleTitle: Asynchronous Hierarchical Federated Learning: Enhancing Communication Efficiency and Scalability
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: This study introduces Asynchronous Hierarchical Federated Learning (FedAH), a novel framework designed to tackle communication bottlenecks and scalability challenges in federated learning (FL) systems. By integrating asynchronous updates with a hierarchical communication structure, FedAH reduces the computational load on the central server, accelerates convergence, and addresses client heterogeneity. Experiments conducted on the CIFAR-10 dataset using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) demonstrate that FedAH achieves faster convergence and significantly lowers communication overhead compared to synchronous methods. However, it also introduces challenges related to system stability, highlighting the need for optimization of learning rates and hyperparameters. Future work will focus on enhancing system stability and scalability through refined hyperparameter tuning and expanding evaluations to diverse datasets and architectures to validate the framework’s generalizability. FedAH represents a promising advancement in efficient and scalable federated learning systems, paving the way for broader applicability in large-scale distributed networks.

articleTitle: MamKanformer: A hybrid Mamba and KAN model based on Medformer for Medical Time-Series Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: The rapid advancements in sensing technology and artificial intelligence have spurred a substantial number of novel demands and challenges within the realm of medical time series analysis. Notably, the effective extraction and utilization of the long-term and short-term dependency relationships, along with the features at various granularities encapsulated within high-dimensional and multivariate time series, have emerged as one of the pressing issues that demand immediate resolution. To address these, we propose a deep learning model MamKanformer for multichannel EEG signal processing. The model firstly solves the problem of long-short term dependencies which are difficult to be modeled effectively by Feed Forward in Transformer by using Mamba architecture. Subsequently, Kan is utilized to capture the critical feature information of different granularities contained in the time series data to assist in enhancing the output of the model. Finally, extensive experiments conducted on three public datasets have effectively verified the efficacy of the method proposed in this paper. Specifically, the MamKanformer model has demonstrated a superior performance over the other 11 baselines. It has achieved an average top ranking across all six metrics within the three datasets, which unequivocally attests to the outstanding capabilities of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Attention-Based Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of Deepfakes technologies, generating highly realistic manipulated videos has become increasingly accessible, raising serious social and security concerns. To overcome the limitations of traditional models, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs), in capturing temporal dependencies across video frames, this paper proposes a Deepfakes detection method using Spatiotemporal Attention mechanisms based on TimeSformer. Our approach detects subtle manipulations and temporal inconsistencies in videos more effectively than conventional methods. By applying transfer learning and fine-tuning in the DFDC and FaceForensics++ datasets, the proposed model achieved an AUC of 0.95 and an F1 score of 86% in FaceForensics++, along with an accuracy of 88% in DFDC. Precise facial region extraction, improved inference strategies, and optimized loss functions further improved performance and generalization across datasets. The experimental outcomes highlight the potential of Spatiotemporal Attention-Based Models for reliable video forgery detection, contributing to the authenticity and security of digital media.

articleTitle: Driver Drowsiness Detection Using Support Vector Machine (SVM) Model from Brain Alpha Wave and GUI Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Driver drowsiness is a major cause of road accidents, especially for long-distance drivers, making monitoring and intervention essential. This paper proposes a novel method for detecting driver drowsiness using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) model and a graphical user interface (GUI). We use electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to measure brain alpha waves indicating drowsiness, extracting features to train an SVM classifier to distinguish between drowsy and alert states. The GUI displays the driver’s drowsiness level and provides visual feedback. Evaluated on 12 drivers, our method achieves 99% accuracy, outperforming existing methods, and can be applied to real-time detection systems.

articleTitle: FDDA-Unet: A Frequency-Domain-based Lightweight Network Used for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Enhancing segmentation performance is the goal of several medical image segmentation techniques. However, these methods often come with a significant increase in the number of parameters and computer complexity, which limits their practical application, especially on edge devices. To address this issue, a lightweight segmentation network, namely Frequency-Domain Dual Attention U-net (FDDA-Unet), was proposed. The proposed network was mainly composed of a Frequency-Domain Dual Attention (FDDA) Block and a Double Depthwise Separable Convolution (DDSC) Block. The proposed model can acquire frequency-domain mixed attention thanks to the FDDA Block, which can enhance feature extraction capabilities and lead to improved model performance in the lightweight model. In addition, the DDSC Block located at the decoder of the model also can reduce the parameters and computations of the network since it processes the size of the feature map and its channels separately. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed FDDA-Unet outperformed other segmentation models in terms of performance with fewer parameters, computations, and Dice similarity coefficient. Consequently, the FDDA Block and DDSC Block have been employed in the proposed model that achieves competitive results in medical image segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: Estimation of Mango Canopy Nitrogen Content in Complex Backgrounds Using UAV Hyperspectral Imaging: A Fusion Method of Adaptive Pixel Weighting and Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: The hyperspectral data of mango canopies collected by UAVs are susceptible to interference from complex environmental factors. This study proposes a spectral feature selection method based on adaptive pixel weight optimization (SWA) to effectively extract key spectral signals from complex backgrounds, thereby enhancing the accuracy of the nitrogen content estimation model for mango canopies. Additionally, ensemble learning methods were introduced to further improve the prediction accuracy of nitrogen content. The results demonstrate that the SWA method significantly enhanced the correlation between spectral data and nitrogen content, increasing the correlation coefficient for reflectance in the 400-900 nm wavelength range to 0.5. After SWA denoising, the ensemble learning models outperformed traditional machine learning models, with the RF+SVR model showing the best performance under the stacking strategy, achieving an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.95 on the test set and reducing the root mean square error (RMSE) to 0.45 mg/g. These results indicate that this method has high predictive accuracy and generalization capability for estimating nitrogen content in mango canopies.

articleTitle: Fast HTNet: Leveraging Subtle Movements for Efficient Micro-expression Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: This paper introduces the Fast Hierarchical Transformer Network (Fast HTNet) for micro-expression recognition. Building on the original HTNet model, Fast HTNet divides the face into three key regions: the eye area, the nose area, and the mouth area. The approach leverages transformer layers to convert local temporal features and employs an aggregation layer to extract both local and global semantic facial features, effectively facilitating micro-expression recognition. While HTNet excels in accuracy, its high computational complexity and low operational efficiency hinder real-time applications. Fast HTNet addresses these limitations by significantly reducing computational resource consumption and operational speed, leading to a substantial decrease in model parameters. Experiments conducted on three publicly available micro-expression datasets demonstrate that Fast HTNet achieves an 87.43% reduction in model parameters and a 46.16% decrease in Floating Point Operations. Notably, the SMIC dataset exhibited the most significant improvements, with UF1 and UAR scores increasing by 3.2% and 5.5%, respectively, while both the SAMM and CASME II datasets showed improvements in UF1 and UAR scores exceeding 1.5%.

articleTitle: Elevating Predictions: Sculpting Flight Delay Predictions with Recursive Feature Elimination
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of the aviation industry and the significant growth of aviation data, how to use big data technology to accurately predict flight delays has become a problem that needs to be solved in the civil aviation transportation industry, and the application of big data models in the aviation field has also become crucial. To address this challenge, a new combinatorial forecasting method is proposed in this study. This method integrates random forest algorithm and recursive feature elimination technology to construct a comprehensive prediction model, aiming at improving the accuracy and efficiency of flight delay prediction. Experiments show that the proposed method performs better in the prediction accuracy and prediction error of flight delay data after the data is normalized to eliminate the influence of different dimensions and magnitudes on the model performance, which proves the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis of ANN and XGBoost Algorithm with WPD in exploring the application of Artificial Intelligence in condition monitoring for oil and gas industries
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: There are considerable benefits to applying Artificial Intelligence (AI) to automation in modern industries, including oil and gas. Oil and Gas Industries have many complex systems in their production and flow line. Condition monitoring of oil and gas equipment provides the fault diagnosis of components, machines, systems, equipment, data hardware, and even software. The predictive maintenance and industry 4.0 applications have more advantages in petrochemical industries to make a safer economic environment. To understand the effectiveness of AI in condition monitoring for oil and gas industries, a case study related to the condition monitoring of drilling machines is conducted, and an ANN and XG Boost ensemble algorithm is used to analyze and predict potential failures. In the signal collection, acoustic emission sensors, signal conditioning devices, NI-data acquisition cards, and LabVIEW software were used. The dataset was collected using a healthy tool, a worn tool, and a tool with a broken tip. The novelty of this work is the proposal of an approach for tool wear monitoring in drilling using acoustic emission sensors and considering Wavelet Packet Decomposition (WPD) for further analysis for feature extraction. The extracted features from WPD are given as input for the ANN and XG Boost Algorithm for classification to identify the health of the drill bit and machine. The result shows that the prediction accuracy is higher in the XG Boost algorithm than ANN. Average accuracy of 94% is achieved in XG Boost whereas a 90% average accuracy is achieved in ANN. So, a detailed analysis has been made to compare the ANN and XG Boost performance, finding the effectiveness of AI-based condition monitoring in enhancing the monitoring effectiveness and equipment safety in Oil and Gas Industries.

articleTitle: Enhanced Neuromorphic Object Detection with Improved CNN and Flash Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Traditional object detection models exhibit limited efficacy in identifying spike camera images, frequently failing to accurately detect target objects with high confidence. They are also characterized by slow training and inference processes, coupled with suboptimal resource utilization. This study introduces an innovative method for the spike camera images object detection that leverages the "Flash Attention" mechanism, which has been effectively validated on the YOLO detection model. This method integrates a sophisticated self-attention layer into the model, significantly enhancing its capacity to process features of diverse sizes, shapes, and complexities. It effectively mitigates the deficiencies of current models in accurately recognizing the high-speed spike camera image under challenging lighting conditions, accelerating both training and inference times and optimizing resource utilization. Consequently, this advancement positions the model as a promising candidate for future applications in the high-speed spike camera image object detection.Our Flash Attention-augmented detection model achieved a notable mean Average Precision (mAP) score of 88% on the spike camera image dataset, marking a 31% improvement in training speed and a 21% increase in inference speed over the baseline model.

articleTitle: FedDPP: A Decentralized Peer-to-Peer Federated Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: The promise of maintaining a high classification accuracy while still achieving low communication and per-node computation cost, remains a central area of concern in federated learning protocols. We propose FedDPP, a Federated Decentralized Peer-to-Peer Mentor-Student learning framework, that is based on peer-to-peer communication among the neighbouring nodes. In this protocol, a node first queries the softmax values of an unlabeled data point for a random class label from its neighbours. Based on these values it identifies a superior mentor and adopts its parameters. The parameters are then retrained with local data. This leads to successful knowledge distillation across the network over the epochs with a small communication cost and without needing a central server to manage aggregation and communication. Experimental results show comparable accuracy across nodes while significantly reducing the overall training time by up to 2.5x and data communicated over the network by up to 3.5x in comparison to established federated learning setups.

articleTitle: A Behavior Recognition Algorithm Based on Global Context Awareness and Pose Information and Its Application in University
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Behavior recognition is an important technology for computer systems to recognize and understand human activities. As an important research topic in computer vision, it has significant application value in areas such as education, human-computer interaction, medical rehabilitation, and autonomous driving. However, in examination scenarios, the complexity of the scene, numerous interference factors, and lack of public datasets lead to poor performance in current mainstream behavior recognition methods. To address this, this paper proposed a behavior recognition model for university students in examination settings based on global context awareness and behavior pose information. This model considers the issue of diminishing examination behavior features with increasing network depth and leverages the advantage of Transformers in capturing long-range dependencies to design a global context information module. It uses behavior pose information that complements visual descriptions to capture high-level behavior information from deep features. To validate the model's effectiveness, an examination behavior dataset was constructed, and experiments were conducted. Experimental results show that the proposed model demonstrates superior performance.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term Wind Power Prediction Based on Bayesian Optimisation XGboost-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence approaches are used in the realm of energy security to increase wind power prediction accuracy and lessen the effect of wind energy uncertainty on wind power generation. Model performance and input features are significantly correlated, which is expected given the temporal, periodic, and non-stationary nature of wind power impacting factors. An ultrashort-term wind power prediction model based on the Bayesian optimization of the XGboost-LSTM is developed in order to enhance the model’s generalization performance and prediction capacity as well as to offer dependable and stable prediction data for wind power generation. First, the model input features are extracted using the extreme gradient boosting tree (XGboost) approach. Second, the entire XGboost-LSTM model is optimized using the Bayesian hyperparameter tuning approach. Finally, by integrating the example data of a wind farm in Bili-uhe, Inner Mongolia, the method’s correctness and efficacy are confirmed by contrasting it with other combined models and a single model. By using the MAE, RMSE, MAPE, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the fitting effect of the wind power curve as the indexes, the results demonstrate that the suggested model has a better fitting effect on the original data and a higher prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Training System for Customer Service Representatives Using Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: This paper introduces an advanced multi-modal training system aimed at enhancing the performance of customer service representatives (CSRs) in managing various customer complaints. This system incorporates large language model (LLM) technology, text-to-speech (TTS) technology and speech-to-text conversion. This combination enables realistic simulations of both logical and illogical customer complaints, crucial for thorough CSRs training. Furthermore, the system features an intelligent coaching agent that assesses trainee responses using advanced customer service theories, offering immediate feedback and actionable insights. When tested in a large call center, the system showed substantial improvements in trainee performance, customer satisfaction, and the resolution rate of customer complaints. These results highlight the potential of multi-modal LLM-based training systems to transform training methodologies in the customer service sector <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>.

articleTitle: Online forecast of ultra-short term wind power based on GWO-OL-OR-ELM
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Continuously increasing installed capacity and large fluctuations in wind power output have a negative impact on the energy supply. However, the limitations of static models lead to their limited generalization ability and robustness in ultra-short term wind power prediction. In this paper, we propose an online prediction based on gray wolf optimization algorithm (GWO), online adaptive learning rate (OL), and online recurrent extreme learning machine (OR-ELM) for online prediction of ultra-short term wind power. First, a multi-layer self-coding online sequential extreme learning machine is used to build a static pre-training model. Then, GWO and OL algorithms are introduced to balance the convergence speed and generalization ability of the model. Finally, the incremental updating of output weights is realized by establishing an online wind power prediction method based on GWO-OL-OR-ELM with incremental updating mechanism. The results show that the method performs better than the traditional method and effectively mitigates the effects of wind power output fluctuations.

articleTitle: Multi-Source Shortest Paths Mining Algorithm for Unweighted Directed Graphs Based on Rough Sets Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Shortest path mining is one of the classic problems in graph theory. How to design an efficient multi-source shortest paths mining algorithm has practical significance. In this article, an efficient multi-source shortest paths algorithm is designed based on rough sets theory. Firstly, within the framework of rough sets theory, investigation has been conducted on the multisource shortest paths, providing a theoretical basis for calculating multi-source shortest paths. Secondly, the R-related set operator is used to search all vertices reachable from each source vertex. Meanwhile, the k-step upper approximation operator is used to search for all vertices that can reach the target vertex. Then, a marking strategy is designed to control the construction of multi-source shortest paths, which can improve the mining efficiency. Finally, a multi-source shortest paths algorithm for unweighted directed graphs (RMSSP) based on rough sets theory is proposed. Experimental results show that the RMSSP algorithm can accurately discover multi-source shortest paths for unweighted directed graphs. Also, it performs better than similar algorithms in terms of computational efficiency. With the expansion of the dataset size, the efficiency advantage of RMSSP algorithm is more obvious.

articleTitle: Multi-feature fusion network: Hand pose estimation for hand-object interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Hand-object interaction often involves significant occlusion of the hand, making this task particularly challenging. Recently, many studies have made substantial progress in predicting hand pose despite severe occlusions, either by directly predicting hand mesh vertices or by utilizing a priori hand models. However, most of these studies overlook the implicit hand features in the occluded regions, which affects the accuracy of the results. To address this issue, we propose a 3D hand pose estimation method called the Multi-Feature Fusion Network. This network learns the correlation between hand features and object occlusion features, utilizing the occluded region information to refine the hand global features, and extracts the hand local features at the same time. Through the joint guidance of multiple features, an accurate hand pose is reconstructed. Extensive experiments on hand-object interaction datasets with severe occlusion problems (HO3D, DEXYCB, and FreiHAND) demonstrate that our approach is highly competitive.

articleTitle: Research on Interpretable Recommendation Methods for Civil Aviation Ancillary Services
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: In the modern civil aviation industry, with the escalating market competition and the increasing diversification of airline profit models, revenue from ancillary services has become a key factor for airlines to enhance their overall revenue and profitability. Leveraging existing mature artificial intelligence technologies, insights into passengers' travel preferences and consumption patterns can be derived from their historical behavioral data, providing precise recommendations for ancillary services with interpretable output results to assist in decision-making processes. Based on this, a deep neural network with interpretability is proposed in this paper. By integrating full attention to capture hidden patterns in passenger behavior, the model's interpretability and recommendation accuracy are enhanced. Additionally, the use of residual structures effectively addresses the issue of gradient vanishing in traditional neural networks, subsequently improving recommendation accuracy and model convergence speed. Experimental validation on real datasets has demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Furthermore, this paper provides an outlook on future research directions.

articleTitle: Order-Based Quantitative Inference for Swarm Drone Estimation in Dynamic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: In dynamic adversarial environments, the uncertainty in the number of drones deployed by the attacking side within the defender’s territory complicates the counter-drone operations for the defense. Traditional detection methods yield incomplete information, making it difficult for the defense to infer the number of attacking drones and to adapt to the demands of battlefield uncertainty. With limited battlefield information, accurately estimating the number of attacking drones is crucial for optimizing weapon deployment strategies. To address this issue, this section employs a First-Come, First-Served (FCFS) GI/G/c queuing model to simulate the inference process of drone numbers in a dynamic environment. Furthermore, this paper introduces an order-based estimation method to handle the problem of drone number inference in uncertain environments. This innovative approach is capable of inferring the number of drones based on partially observable data. The study also evaluates the effectiveness of this method in different scenarios for inferring the number of various types of drones. To test the robustness of the method, noise is introduced during the inference process in this paper, and its impact is verified. Simulation results demonstrate that the method can effectively infer the number of attacking drones in a battlefield environment with uncertainty, providing strategic support for counter-drone strategies.

articleTitle: Improving Few-Shot Code Generation with Prompt Selection and Augmentation Techniques in Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Few-shot prompting and step-by-step reasoning have enhanced the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) in tackling complex tasks including code generation. In this paper, we introduce a prompt selection and augmentation algorithm aimed at improving mathematical reasoning and robot arm operations. Our approach incorporates a multi-stage example augmentation scheme combined with an example selection scheme. This algorithm improves LLM performance by selecting a set of examples that increase diversity, minimize redundancy, and increase relevance to the question. When combined with the Program-of-Thought prompting, our algorithm demonstrates an improvement in performance on the GSM8K and SVAMP benchmarks, with increases of 0.3% and 1.1% respectively. Furthermore, in simulated tabletop environments, our algorithm surpasses the Code-as-Policies approach by achieving a 3.4% increase in successful task completions and a decrease of over 70% in the number of examples used. Its ability to discard examples that contribute little to solving the problem reduces the inferencing time of an LLM-powered robotics system. This algorithm also offers important benefits for industrial process automation by streamlining the development and deployment process, reducing manual programming effort, and enhancing code reusability.

articleTitle: Identification of Crystallization State of Ammonium Nitrate Aqueous Solution Based on EfficientNet Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: The quality of aqueous ammonium nitrate solutions is a crucial factor affecting the production quality of industrial explosives. Accurate identification of crystallization states and precise recording of crystallization temperatures in these solutions are of paramount importance during the manufacturing process. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), leveraging the principle of "translation invariance" in images, can effectively learn salient features, making them suitable for addressing the problem of automatic detection of crystallization states in aqueous ammonium nitrate solutions. This study proposes EfficientNet-blast, an optimized algorithm based on EfficientNet, specifically designed for this purpose.EfficientNet-blast utilizes deep neural network architecture, EfficientNet, with integrated Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) modules as its foundation. By increasing the number of feature channels in each layer while strategically removing multiple MBConv layers in depth, the model reduces the number of parameters, lowers FLOPS (Floating Point Operations), and accelerates detection. After training on a curated dataset of crystallization states, EfficientNet-blast achieves a remarkable recognition accuracy of 99.83% thanks to its improved convolutional and pooling characteristics.A comparative analysis of EfficientNet-blast with existing image recognition algorithms such as ResNet-50, MobileNetV2, ShuffleNet, DenseNet, EfficientNet, and Swin Transformer, using the same crystallization state dataset, reveals that EfficientNet-blast comprehensively enhances accuracy while maintaining a relatively low parameter count and without significantly increasing FLOPs. It sustains a high detection speed, with FPS (Frames Per Second) consistently at a level suitable for real-time monitoring. The experimental results show that the algorithm EfficientNet-blast can quickly and accurately identify the crystallization state, and the measurement deviation of the crystallization point temperature is less than or equal to ±0.3℃. The measured crystallization point temperature dispersion degree is small, the measurement fluctuation value is small, and the stability is high. This study offers a practical solution for enhancing quality control in industrial explosives production and holds promising applications in related fields.

articleTitle: From Complex Network Perspective: Is Anecdotal Inference in Social Network Effective?
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Anecdotes play a significant role in human communication and understanding. Inference on individual experiences and isolated cases is defined as anecdotal inference here. This study employs complex network methods to model the anecdotal inference to four small-scale sampling algorithm. The limitation is verified through theoretical derivation and numerical simulation. Theoretical result is marked by bias between the expected value, positively correlated with high-degree nodes’ attributes, and the latent parameters. Experimental result is shown by comparing results error of the algorithms in scale-free, small-world, random, and CNN network models, and the results validate the theoretical conclusion. Additionally, different network structural properties show varying influence on the error of estimated value.

articleTitle: Enhancing the robustness of Fast-DetectGPT against paraphrase attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been able to generate high-quality text and demonstrate excellent performance in various tasks. However, the ability of large language models to generate increasingly efficient human like texts has also raised concerns about their misuse for malicious purposes. Therefore, it is urgent to design a reliable and robust method for generating text detection. The zero-shot detector Fast-DetectGPT not only demonstrates strong performance in detection accuracy, but is also commendable in detection speed. However, it is unclear whether it can still maintain such a high detection success rate in the face of paraphrase attacks. In this article, we use various paraphrase attacks to perturb text and evaluate the robustness of Fast-DetectGPT, and find a significant decrease in its performance. Meanwhile, we propose Sentence-DetectGPT to optimize the detection process of Fast-DetectGPT, greatly enhancing its robustness in the face of paraphrase attacks.

Index Terms: Performance In A Variety Of Tasks

articleTitle: An Integrated Strategy for Accelerating Attribute Reduction in Neighborhood Rough Set
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: Neighborhood rough set model has received much attention in Granular Computing due to its ability to show the process of information granulation more intuitively. As an important application of this model, the problems related to attribute reduction have also attracted wide attention, especially its time consumption. To reduce the time consumption, various acceleration algorithms have been proposed. However, most of the existing acceleration algorithms accelerate the procedure of deriving reduct from only one perspective of the sample or conditional attribute, so the acceleration efficiency still needs to be improved. In order to solve this problem, this paper accelerates from the integrated perspectives of sample and conditional attribute and then proposes a new attribute reduction algorithm. First, the samples are randomly divided into multiple sample subsets and then sorted in ascending order based on their granularities, the higher the order, the finer its granularity. Next, the granularities of the conditional attributes within each sample subset are calculated and these conditional attributes are also sorted in ascending order of granularity. For the sample subsets with the same sorting results of conditional attributes, one of the subsets will be retained randomly. Finally, the reduct is obtained from the finest granularity sample subset by sequentially adding conditional attributes to the reduct pool based on granularity, which guides the coarser granularity sample subset. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, it is compared with four acceleration algorithms using 9 UCI data sets. The results show that the proposed algorithm has superior performance in both execution efficiency and the quality of reduct.

articleTitle: A Study on Task Offloading Based on Multi-Agent Advantage Actor Critic Algorithms in IIoT
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of Industry 4.0, resource-constrained industrial devices are often unable to meet different demands of compute-intensive and latency-sensitive tasks in modern factories. To cope with this challenge, offloading tasks from industrial devices to edge servers or a cloud computing center to obtain lower delay is a good solution. Most of the traditional task offloading approaches rely on centralized decision-making systems, which may not be able to efficiently cope with device heterogeneity and the specific needs of different tasks in industrial environments. To address this problem, this study proposes a more comprehensive edge computing network model for Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). By integrating an action masking technique, we establish a Markov decision model with a constrained action space. Additionally, we propose a task offloading framework based on the Multi-Agent Advantage Actor Critic (MAA2C) algorithm, adopting the Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE) architecture, aiming to achieve task offloading decision-making in modern factories and reduce the overall system delay. Validated through numerical simulation experiments, our proposed framework not only performs well in reducing system delay but also shows good adaptability in different industrial environments.
